T02_HV.q: Per IEC 60092, what voltage is considered 'High Voltage' on ships?
T02_HV.a: Above 1000V AC or 1500V DC
T02_HV.exp: IEC 60092 defines Low Voltage as up to and including 1000V AC. High Voltage is anything above 1000V AC or 1500V DC.

T02_HV.q: What is the primary advantage of using High Voltage on ships with large electrical demand?
T02_HV.a: Lower current for the same power, resulting in smaller cables and reduced weight
opts: Lower current for the same power, resulting in smaller cables and reduced weight
T02_HV.exp: Power = V x I x √3. Doubling the voltage halves the current for the same power, significantly reducing cable size, weight, and I²R losses.

T02_HV.q: Why are standard ship HV voltages (3.3kV, 6.6kV, 11kV) multiples of 1.1?
T02_HV.a: Derived from the form factor (1.11) of a sinusoidal AC waveform and IEC standard series
opts: It matches the frequency of 60Hz exactly
Derived from the form factor (1.11) of a sinusoidal AC waveform and IEC standard series

T02_HV.q: Why is an Air Circuit Breaker (ACB) generally not used for High Voltage systems?
T02_HV.a: Air ionises under intense HV arc energy and fails to quench the arc
opts: Air ionises under intense HV arc energy and fails to quench the arc
Air reacts with copper at high voltage

T02_HV.q: How does a Vacuum Circuit Breaker (VCB) quench an electrical arc?
T02_HV.a: Contacts open in a vacuum; metal vapour arc dissipates instantly at the first current zero crossing
opts: It stretches the arc using magnetic chutes
It blasts air to cool the contacts
Contacts open in a vacuum; metal vapour arc dissipates instantly at the first current zero crossing
It uses SF6 gas to absorb electrons
T02_HV.exp: In a vacuum (no air molecules to ionise), the small metal vapour arc formed during opening dissipates instantly when the AC current crosses zero.

T02_HV.q: What is a major property of SF6 (Sulphur Hexafluoride) gas used in switchgear?
T02_HV.a: It is electronegative and absorbs free electrons, preventing arc sustaining
opts: It is electronegative and absorbs free electrons, preventing arc sustaining
It is a highly conductive plasma
T02_HV.exp: SF6 is strongly electronegative. It captures free electrons to form heavy, immobile negative ions, rapidly increasing dielectric strength and quenching the arc.

T02_HV.q: What is a critical environmental and safety concern regarding SF6 gas?

It is highly corrosive to copper
It is explosive when mixed with air
T02_HV.exp: SF6 has a GWP of 23,500x CO₂. Furthermore, when exposed to an electric arc, it decomposes into highly toxic gases like HF and SOF2.

To keep the control circuit connected
T02_HV.exp: Racking a closed breaker would interrupt massive load or fault currents in open air rather than inside the vacuum bottle, causing an explosive arc flash.

To limit earth fault current to a safe low value (typically 5-30A) and prevent overvoltages

T02_HV.q: What is an 'Arc Flash'?
T02_HV.a: An explosive release of energy and intense heat (>20,000°C) from an electrical arc fault through air
opts: A controlled spark used to test insulation
An explosive release of energy and intense heat (>20,000°C) from an electrical arc fault through air
The bright light emitted by a VCB operating normally
A static discharge between two ungrounded objects
T02_HV.exp: Arc flash is a catastrophic fault producing intense radiant heat, blinding UV light, and vaporised metal.

T02_HV.q: What phenomenon typically accompanies an Arc Flash and can throw personnel across a room?
T02_HV.a: Arc Blast (pressure/shock wave from rapid air expansion)
opts: Arc Blast (pressure/shock wave from rapid air expansion)
T02_HV.exp: Arc Blast is the physical pressure wave caused by the rapid expansion of air and vaporised metal (copper expands 67,000 times its volume).

T02_HV.q: What is the most critical first step before performing any maintenance on a High Voltage system?
T02_HV.a: Perform a Risk Assessment and obtain a Permit to Work (PTW)
opts: Perform a Risk Assessment and obtain a Permit to Work (PTW)
T02_HV.exp: HV work ALWAYS begins with a formal risk assessment and obtaining an authorised Permit to Work. No exceptions.

T02_HV.q: Why must you wait at least 5 minutes after isolating an HV circuit before working on it?
T02_HV.a: To allow the lethal capacitive charge stored in HV cables and equipment to fully dissipate
opts: To let the equipment cool down
To allow the lethal capacitive charge stored in HV cables and equipment to fully dissipate
To allow SF6 gas to settle
To ensure the VCB mechanism resets
T02_HV.exp: HV cables have high capacitance and act like giant capacitors. Even after disconnection from supply, they retain a lethal charge that takes time to drain.

T02_HV.q: When testing for dead on an isolated HV circuit, what is the correct testing sequence?
T02_HV.a: Test on known live source → Test isolated circuit (all phases to earth) → Retest on known live source
opts: Test on known live source → Test isolated circuit (all phases to earth) → Retest on known live source

T02_HV.exp: Class 2 (Yellow) is standard for 6.6kV systems. Class 3 (Green) is used for 11kV systems. Gloves must be tested every 6 months.

T02_HV.q: What must always be worn over HV rubber insulating gloves?
T02_HV.a: Leather outer protectors
opts: Nothing, they must be used alone
T02_HV.exp: Rubber insulating gloves are very susceptible to cuts and punctures. Leather outer protectors shield the rubber from mechanical damage.

T02_HV.q: Why is a 2500V or 5000V megger used for testing 6.6kV HV equipment instead of a 500V megger?
T02_HV.a: To meaningfully stress the thick HV insulation to a level comparable to its operating voltage and detect weak spots
opts: To meaningfully stress the thick HV insulation to a level comparable to its operating voltage and detect weak spots
To overcome the high resistance of HV copper
To charge the cable capacitance faster
T02_HV.exp: A 500V test on 6.6kV insulation applies less than 8% of operating stress. It will pass severely degraded insulation that would instantly fail under actual 6.6kV stress.

T02_HV.q: What is the general rule of thumb for the MINIMUM acceptable insulation resistance (IR) for HV equipment?
T02_HV.a: Rated Voltage (in kV) + 1 Megohm
T02_HV.exp: Minimum IR = kV + 1 MΩ. For 6.6kV equipment, the absolute minimum is 7.6 MΩ. For 11kV, it is 12 MΩ.

T02_HV.q: What does the '200% insulation' standard require before returning HV equipment to service after repair?
T02_HV.a: Measured IR must be at least twice the minimum acceptable value
opts: Insulation must be physically twice as thick
Measured IR must be at least twice the minimum acceptable value
Two layers of rubber tape must be used
T02_HV.exp: 200% insulation means a safety margin. If the minimum allowed is 1 MΩ, the repaired equipment must measure at least 2 MΩ before it is deemed safe.

T02_HV.q: Recall: What does the '200% insulation' standard require before returning HV equipment to service after repair?
T02_HV.a: Measured IR must be at least twice the minimum acceptable value
opts: Measured IR must be at least twice the minimum acceptable value
Two layers of rubber tape must be used
Insulation must be physically twice as thick
T02_HV.exp: 200% insulation means a safety margin. If the minimum allowed is 1 MΩ, the repaired equipment must measure at least 2 MΩ before it is deemed safe.

opts: To overcome the high resistance of HV copper
To charge the cable capacitance faster
To meaningfully stress the thick HV insulation to a level comparable to its operating voltage and detect weak spots

T02_HV.a: Injects a low-voltage signal between neutral and earth and monitors the circuit impedance

Measures the neutral voltage to earth

T02_HV.q: In tanker electrical zones, what is Zone 0?
T02_HV.a: An area where a flammable atmosphere is continuously present (e.g., inside cargo tanks)
opts: An area where flammable atmosphere is likely during normal operation
An area where flammable atmosphere is unlikely
An area where a flammable atmosphere is continuously present (e.g., inside cargo tanks)
T02_HV.exp: Zone 0 is the most hazardous. Only Category 'ia' Intrinsically Safe (Ex-ia) equipment is permitted in Zone 0.

T02_HV.q: What is the correct sequence for bonding and connecting hoses during tanker cargo operations?
T02_HV.a: Connect ship-to-jetty bonding cable FIRST, then connect cargo hose. (Disconnect in reverse order).
opts: Connect hose first, then bonding cable
Connect ship-to-jetty bonding cable FIRST, then connect cargo hose. (Disconnect in reverse order).
Bonding is not required for modern tankers
Connect hose, start pumping, then connect bonding cable
T02_HV.exp: The ship and jetty must be brought to the same electrical potential BEFORE the hose flanges come near each other, preventing static sparks from igniting vapours.

T02_HV.q: What is the principle behind 'Ex-d' (Flameproof) equipment used in Zone 1 areas?
T02_HV.a: The heavy enclosure contains any internal explosion and cools escaping gases via long flame paths below ignition temperature
opts: It prevents any gas from entering the enclosure
It limits the circuit energy so sparks cannot ignite gas
The heavy enclosure contains any internal explosion and cools escaping gases via long flame paths below ignition temperature
It is constantly purged with fresh air
T02_HV.exp: Ex-d doesn't stop gas getting in. It allows internal explosions but ensures the flame cannot propagate outside the enclosure to the surrounding atmosphere.

T02_HV.exp: The bearing oil film insulates the shaft. Stray common-mode currents (from alternators or VFDs) build up voltage and arc through the oil film, destroying the bearings. The shaft earthing brush safely bypasses this current to the hull.

T02_HV.q: According to Surveyor Kamath, what is the required IR value for an HV motor (e.g. 6.6kV) before starting?
T02_HV.a: (Un/1000) + 1 Megohm, so minimum 7.6 Megohms (often practical rule is >100 MΩ)
opts: (Un/1000) + 1 Megohm, so minimum 7.6 Megohms (often practical rule is >100 MΩ)
T02_HV.exp: Surveyor specific HV question.

T02_HV.q: Surveyor Deswal usually asks: How is the arc extinguished in a Vacuum Circuit Breaker (VCB)?
T02_HV.a: By interrupting the current in a high vacuum where no ionizable gas exists
opts: By interrupting the current in a high vacuum where no ionizable gas exists
T02_HV.exp: Surveyor specific HV question.

T02_HV.q: What is the significance of the Polarization Index (PI) test in HV cables as requested by surveyors?
T02_HV.a: It indicates the cleanliness and dryness of the insulation over time (10 min / 1 min ratio)
opts: It indicates the cleanliness and dryness of the insulation over time (10 min / 1 min ratio)
T02_HV.exp: Surveyor specific HV question.

T02_HV.q: What happens if a vacuum bottle in a VCB loses its vacuum? (Common surveyor question)
T02_HV.a: The arc cannot be extinguished and the breaker may violently explode if operated under load
opts: The arc cannot be extinguished and the breaker may violently explode if operated under load
T02_HV.exp: Surveyor specific HV question.

T02_HV.q: According to MMD Surveyors, what is the most critical safety document required before commencing HV maintenance?
T02_HV.a: Permit to Work (PTW)
T02_HV.exp: Surveyor specific HV question.

T02_HV.q: What is the function of the corona shield in high voltage systems?
T02_HV.a: To evenly distribute electric field and prevent corona discharge
opts: To evenly distribute electric field and prevent corona discharge
T02_HV.exp: Surveyor specific HV question.

T02_HV.q: Surveyor Sanjib asks: How do you prove a high voltage circuit is dead?
T02_HV.a: By using an approved and tested Voltage Indicating Device (VID)
opts: By using an approved and tested Voltage Indicating Device (VID)
T02_HV.exp: Surveyor specific HV question.

T02_HV.q: During an oral exam, how would you explain 'Sanction to Test' for HV systems?
T02_HV.a: A formal document allowing testing on HV equipment without a full PTW for operational checks
opts: A formal document allowing testing on HV equipment without a full PTW for operational checks
T02_HV.exp: Surveyor specific HV question.

T02_HV.q: What is the minimum safe distance (clearance) when working near exposed 6.6kV conductors?
T02_HV.a: Usually minimum 1 meter for 6.6kV, depending on company SMS
opts: Usually minimum 1 meter for 6.6kV, depending on company SMS
T02_HV.exp: Surveyor specific HV question.

T02_HV.q: Surveyor Deswal asks: Why are HV cables screened with a copper tape or wire?
T02_HV.a: To confine the electric field within the insulation and provide a path for earth fault currents
opts: To confine the electric field within the insulation and provide a path for earth fault currents
T02_HV.exp: Surveyor specific HV question.

T02_HV.q: What is the purpose of a discharge stick in HV maintenance?
T02_HV.a: To safely discharge residual static charge from HV cables to earth before touching
opts: To safely discharge residual static charge from HV cables to earth before touching
T02_HV.exp: Surveyor specific HV question.

T02_HV.q: How do you test an HV voltage indicating device (VID) before use?
T02_HV.a: By testing it on a known live source or using a proving unit before and after use
opts: By testing it on a known live source or using a proving unit before and after use
T02_HV.exp: Surveyor specific HV question.

T02_HV.q: Surveyor Kamath asks: Why do we use vacuum instead of air for 6.6kV breakers?
T02_HV.a: Vacuum has superior dielectric strength and allows very compact breaker designs
opts: Vacuum has superior dielectric strength and allows very compact breaker designs
T02_HV.exp: Surveyor specific HV question.

T02_HV.q: What is the dielectric strength of the vacuum used in VCBs?
T02_HV.a: Typically 10^-5 to 10^-7 torr
T02_HV.exp: Surveyor specific HV question.

T02_HV.q: According to surveyors, why is the NER rated for a specific time limit (e.g. 10 seconds)?
T02_HV.a: To prevent the resistor from melting due to excessive heat during a sustained earth fault
opts: To prevent the resistor from melting due to excessive heat during a sustained earth fault
T02_HV.exp: Surveyor specific HV question.

T02_HV.q: What happens if the HV earth fault is not cleared within the NER rating time?
T02_HV.a: The NER could fail, leading to an uncontrolled earth fault and potential fire
opts: The NER could fail, leading to an uncontrolled earth fault and potential fire
T02_HV.exp: Surveyor specific HV question.

T02_HV.q: Surveyor Sanjib: What is the difference between an Earthing Switch and a Circuit Breaker?
T02_HV.a: Earthing switch is designed to handle fault making current, but not load breaking current
opts: Earthing switch is designed to handle fault making current, but not load breaking current
T02_HV.exp: Surveyor specific HV question.

T02_HV.q: Why must the earthing switch be closed before issuing a Permit to Work?
T02_HV.a: To ensure any accidental energization results in a safe short to ground, protecting workers
opts: To ensure any accidental energization results in a safe short to ground, protecting workers
T02_HV.exp: Surveyor specific HV question.

T02_HV.q: During an MMD exam, how do you describe a 'High Voltage' system limit on ships?
T02_HV.a: Any voltage exceeding 1000V AC or 1500V DC
opts: Any voltage exceeding 1000V AC or 1500V DC
T02_HV.exp: Surveyor specific HV question.

T02_HV.q: What is the primary risk of arc flash in HV switchboards?
T02_HV.a: Severe burns from intense heat, pressure wave, and flying molten metal
opts: Severe burns from intense heat, pressure wave, and flying molten metal
T02_HV.exp: Surveyor specific HV question.

T02_HV.q: Surveyor Deswal asks: What PPE is mandatory for racking out a VCB?
T02_HV.a: Arc flash suit, face shield, and rated HV gloves
opts: Arc flash suit, face shield, and rated HV gloves
T02_HV.exp: Surveyor specific HV question.

T02_HV.q: How do you measure the contact resistance of a VCB?
T02_HV.a: Using a micro-ohmmeter (Ductor tester) injecting DC current
opts: Using a micro-ohmmeter (Ductor tester) injecting DC current
T02_HV.exp: Surveyor specific HV question.

T02_HV.q: What is the significance of tracking in HV insulation?
T02_HV.a: Formation of a permanent conductive path across the surface of insulation
opts: Formation of a permanent conductive path across the surface of insulation
T02_HV.exp: Surveyor specific HV question.

T02_HV.q: According to Surveyor Kamath, what causes corona discharge?
T02_HV.a: Ionization of air around conductors due to concentrated electric fields
opts: Ionization of air around conductors due to concentrated electric fields
T02_HV.exp: Surveyor specific HV question.

T02_HV.q: What is a PTW (Permit to Work) and who issues it for HV?
T02_HV.a: A safety document issued by the Chief Engineer (or authorized HV person)
opts: A safety document issued by the Chief Engineer (or authorized HV person)
T02_HV.exp: Surveyor specific HV question.

T02_HV.q: Surveyor Sanjib: What is the function of the anti-condensation heater in an HV motor?
T02_HV.a: To prevent moisture condensation on windings when the motor is stopped
opts: To prevent moisture condensation on windings when the motor is stopped
T02_HV.exp: Surveyor specific HV question.

T02_HV.q: How is the anti-condensation heater interlocked with the main HV contactor?
T02_HV.a: It is normally closed when the main contactor is open, and vice versa
opts: It is normally closed when the main contactor is open, and vice versa
T02_HV.exp: Surveyor specific HV question.

T02_HV.q: During surveyor exams, what is the accepted value of a PI test that indicates good insulation?
T02_HV.a: A PI value greater than 2.0 indicates good insulation
opts: A PI value greater than 2.0 indicates good insulation
T02_HV.exp: Surveyor specific HV question.

T02_HV.q: What does a PI value below 1.0 indicate according to surveyors?
T02_HV.a: The insulation is dangerously wet or degraded and must not be energized
opts: The insulation is dangerously wet or degraded and must not be energized
T02_HV.exp: Surveyor specific HV question.

T03_Motors.q: What is the primary law governing the induction of EMF in the rotor of an induction motor?
T03_Motors.a: Faraday's Law of Electromagnetic Induction
T03_Motors.exp: Faraday's Law states that an EMF is induced in a conductor when there is a relative change in magnetic flux linkage, which occurs when the RMF cuts the stationary rotor bars.

T03_Motors.q: How far apart are the three-phase windings distributed in the stator of an induction motor?
T03_Motors.a: 120 electrical degrees
T03_Motors.exp: The stator has three distinct windings spaced exactly 120 electrical degrees apart to create a uniform Rotating Magnetic Field (RMF) when fed by a 3-phase supply.

T03_Motors.q: What is the formula to calculate synchronous speed (Ns)?
T03_Motors.a: Ns = 120f / P
T03_Motors.exp: Ns is directly proportional to frequency (f) and inversely proportional to the number of poles (P).

T03_Motors.q: What is the synchronous speed of a 2-pole induction motor on a 60Hz supply?
T03_Motors.a: 3600 RPM

T03_Motors.q: Why is the rotor of an induction motor short-circuited?
T03_Motors.a: To allow the induced EMF to drive a current, which then interacts with the RMF to produce torque
opts: To allow the induced EMF to drive a current, which then interacts with the RMF to produce torque
To provide physical strength to the rotor
To eliminate the need for brushes
T03_Motors.exp: Without a closed circuit, the induced EMF cannot produce a current. Torque (F=BIL) requires a current-carrying conductor in a magnetic field.

T03_Motors.q: Why is it called an 'Induction' motor?
T03_Motors.a: Because rotor current is not supplied directly, but is induced electromagnetically by the stator field
opts: Because it induces a high power factor
Because rotor current is not supplied directly, but is induced electromagnetically by the stator field
Because it uses inductors in the stator
Because it runs at synchronous speed
T03_Motors.exp: Unlike DC motors with commutators or sync motors with slip rings, the standard squirrel cage rotor has no electrical connection to the supply.

T03_Motors.q: What determines the direction of rotation of the Rotating Magnetic Field (RMF)?
T03_Motors.a: The phase sequence of the 3-phase supply
opts: The number of poles in the stator
The phase sequence of the 3-phase supply
T03_Motors.exp: Swapping any two phases changes the phase sequence (e.g., RYB to YRB), which reverses the direction the RMF spins.

T03_Motors.q: Which component constitutes the physical 'air gap' in an induction motor?
T03_Motors.a: The microscopic radial clearance between the stator bore and the rotor outer diameter
opts: The space inside the terminal box
The microscopic radial clearance between the stator bore and the rotor outer diameter
The cooling vents in the frame
T03_Motors.exp: The air gap must be very small (e.g., 0.5mm) to minimize reluctance and ensure strong magnetic coupling.

T03_Motors.q: What happens if the air gap is uneven due to bearing wear?
T03_Motors.a: Unbalanced magnetic pull occurs, causing severe vibration and potential rotor rub
opts: Efficiency improves due to better cooling
Unbalanced magnetic pull occurs, causing severe vibration and potential rotor rub
T03_Motors.exp: The magnetic pull is inversely proportional to the air gap distance. A smaller gap on one side causes a massive pulling force, compounding bearing wear.

T03_Motors.q: What is 'skewing' of rotor slots?
T03_Motors.a: Arranging the rotor bars at a slight angle to the shaft axis rather than parallel to it
opts: Cutting deeper slots to hold more copper
Arranging the rotor bars at a slight angle to the shaft axis rather than parallel to it
Using zigzag shapes for stator windings
T03_Motors.exp: Skewing reduces magnetic hum, smooths out torque ripple, and prevents 'cogging' (magnetic locking between stator and rotor teeth).

T03_Motors.q: What is 'cogging' in an induction motor?
T03_Motors.a: Magnetic locking of the rotor and stator teeth causing failure to start
opts: Magnetic locking of the rotor and stator teeth causing failure to start
High speed vibration caused by bearing failure
The slow crawling of the motor at 1/7th speed
Excessive slipping of the rotor under load
T03_Motors.exp: If the number of stator teeth equals the number of rotor teeth, strong magnetic alignment can occur at standstill, preventing rotation.

T03_Motors.q: What material is typically used for the squirrel cage in standard small marine motors?
T03_Motors.a: Die-cast Aluminium
T03_Motors.exp: Aluminium is lightweight, cheap, and easily die-cast directly into the rotor slots, forming the bars and end rings in one piece.

T03_Motors.q: What is a major advantage of a slip ring (wound rotor) motor over a squirrel cage motor?
T03_Motors.a: External resistance can be added to the rotor circuit to increase starting torque and lower starting current
opts: External resistance can be added to the rotor circuit to increase starting torque and lower starting current
T03_Motors.exp: Slip rings allow access to the rotor circuit. Adding high resistance alters the torque-speed curve, giving maximum torque at starting.

T03_Motors.q: What causes the 'humming' sound in an induction motor?
T03_Motors.a: Magnetostriction of the core laminations and magnetic forces in the air gap
opts: Friction of the air against the rotor
Magnetostriction of the core laminations and magnetic forces in the air gap
T03_Motors.exp: The alternating magnetic field causes tiny expansions and contractions (magnetostriction) in the iron core at twice the supply frequency (100Hz for a 50Hz supply).

T03_Motors.q: What is the typical power factor of an induction motor at no load?
T03_Motors.a: Very low and lagging (e.g., 0.15 to 0.3)
T03_Motors.exp: At no load, the active power drawn is tiny (just to overcome friction), but the reactive magnetising current to sustain the RMF remains large.

T03_Motors.q: What is the typical power factor of an induction motor at full load?
T03_Motors.a: High and lagging (e.g., 0.8 to 0.9)
T03_Motors.exp: As load increases, the active current drawn from the supply increases massively, while the reactive magnetising current stays roughly constant, improving the ratio.

T03_Motors.q: How does an induction motor react to a drop in supply voltage while driving a constant torque load?
T03_Motors.a: It slows down slightly, slip increases, and it draws MORE current to maintain the required power
opts: It draws less current and runs cooler
It slows down slightly, slip increases, and it draws MORE current to maintain the required power
T03_Motors.exp: Since Power = √3 * V * I * PF, if V drops and required Power is constant, current (I) must increase, leading to overheating.

T03_Motors.q: What dictates the actual operating speed of a motor?
T03_Motors.a: The point where the motor's torque-speed curve intersects the load's torque-speed curve
opts: The voltage of the supply alone
The point where the motor's torque-speed curve intersects the load's torque-speed curve
The size of the cooling fan
T03_Motors.exp: The motor accelerates until the torque it produces exactly matches the opposing torque of the driven load (pump, fan, etc).

T03_Motors.q: What is 'pull-out' torque (breakdown torque)?
T03_Motors.a: The maximum absolute torque the motor can develop before it stalls
opts: The torque at exact synchronous speed
The maximum absolute torque the motor can develop before it stalls
The torque required to remove the rotor
The torque during a star-delta transition
T03_Motors.exp: If the mechanical load exceeds the pull-out torque (usually 2-3x full load torque), the motor will rapidly decelerate and stall.

T03_Motors.q: Why are rotor laminations used instead of a solid iron block?
T03_Motors.a: To minimise eddy current losses in the rotor core
opts: To minimise eddy current losses in the rotor core
T03_Motors.exp: Just like transformers, changing magnetic fields induce circulating eddy currents in solid iron, causing massive heating. Thin, insulated laminations break the current path.

T03_Motors.q: In a 3-phase induction motor, how is the RMF's amplitude related to the maximum phase flux (Φm)?
T03_Motors.a: It is constant and equals 1.5 * Φm
opts: It is constant and equals 1.5 * Φm
It pulsates between zero and Φm
T03_Motors.exp: The vector sum of the three alternating phase fluxes creates a resultant flux that is perfectly constant in magnitude (1.5 Φm) and rotates smoothly.

T03_Motors.q: What is the function of the end rings in a squirrel cage rotor?
T03_Motors.a: To electrically short-circuit all the rotor bars together, allowing current to circulate
opts: To electrically short-circuit all the rotor bars together, allowing current to circulate
To provide attachment points for the bearings
T03_Motors.exp: Without the end rings, the rotor bars would be open circuits, preventing any induced current from flowing, resulting in zero torque.

T03_Motors.q: If a surveyor asks 'What creates the torque in an induction motor?', what is the fundamental physics equation?
T03_Motors.a: F = B * I * L (Lorentz Force Law)
opts: F = B * I * L (Lorentz Force Law)
T03_Motors.exp: A current (I) flowing through a rotor bar of length (L) situated in the stator's magnetic field (B) experiences a mechanical force (F).

T03_Motors.a: Faraday's Law of Electromagnetic Induction
T03_Motors.exp: Faraday's Law states that an EMF is induced in a conductor when there is a relative change in magnetic flux linkage, which occurs when the RMF cuts the stationary rotor bars.

Because it induces a high power factor
Because it runs at synchronous speed

T03_Motors.a: The phase sequence of the 3-phase supply
opts: The number of poles in the stator
The phase sequence of the 3-phase supply
T03_Motors.exp: Swapping any two phases changes the phase sequence (e.g., RYB to YRB), which reverses the direction the RMF spins.

T03_Motors.q: What happens if the rotor of an induction motor reaches exact synchronous speed?
T03_Motors.a: Relative motion becomes zero, no EMF is induced, rotor current drops to zero, and torque becomes zero
opts: The motor operates at maximum efficiency
Relative motion becomes zero, no EMF is induced, rotor current drops to zero, and torque becomes zero
T03_Motors.exp: The rotor must always lag the RMF (slip) to ensure flux lines are continuously cut to induce the current required for torque.

T03_Motors.q: What is the mathematical definition of fractional slip (s)?
T03_Motors.a: s = (Ns - N) / Ns
T03_Motors.exp: Slip is the difference between synchronous speed (Ns) and actual rotor speed (N), expressed as a fraction of synchronous speed.

T03_Motors.q: At the exact moment of starting (standstill), what is the value of slip?
T03_Motors.exp: At standstill, rotor speed (N) is zero. Therefore, slip = (Ns - 0) / Ns = 1.

T03_Motors.q: What is the typical full-load slip for a standard squirrel cage motor?
T03_Motors.exp: At full load, the rotor must slow down by 3-8% relative to the RMF to induce enough current to match the mechanical load torque.

T03_Motors.q: How does an increase in mechanical load affect slip and rotor current?
T03_Motors.a: Slip increases, causing more flux cutting, which increases rotor EMF, rotor current, and torque
opts: Slip decreases, causing less rotor current
Slip remains constant, but stator voltage increases
Slip increases, causing more flux cutting, which increases rotor EMF, rotor current, and torque
Slip increases, but rotor current decreases
T03_Motors.exp: To pull a heavier load, the motor must develop more torque. It does this by slowing down slightly (increasing slip), which induces more rotor current.

T03_Motors.q: What is the relationship between supply frequency (f) and rotor frequency (fr)?
T03_Motors.a: fr = s * f
T03_Motors.exp: Rotor frequency depends on the relative speed (slip). At standstill (s=1), fr = f. At normal running (e.g., s=0.04), fr is very low (e.g., 2Hz).

T03_Motors.q: If a 50Hz motor has a slip of 4%, what is the frequency of the currents in the rotor bars?
T03_Motors.a: 2 Hz

T03_Motors.q: Review: What happens if the rotor of an induction motor reaches exact synchronous speed?
T03_Motors.a: Relative motion becomes zero, no EMF is induced, rotor current drops to zero, and torque becomes zero
opts: The motor operates at maximum efficiency
Relative motion becomes zero, no EMF is induced, rotor current drops to zero, and torque becomes zero
T03_Motors.exp: The rotor must always lag the RMF (slip) to ensure flux lines are continuously cut to induce the current required for torque.

T03_Motors.q: Review: What is the mathematical definition of fractional slip (s)?
T03_Motors.a: s = (Ns - N) / Ns
T03_Motors.exp: Slip is the difference between synchronous speed (Ns) and actual rotor speed (N), expressed as a fraction of synchronous speed.

T03_Motors.q: What is the typical Direct-On-Line (DOL) starting current for a standard induction motor?
T03_Motors.a: 5 to 8 times the rated full-load current
opts: 5 to 8 times the rated full-load current
T03_Motors.exp: At standstill (slip=1), the rotor cuts the stator flux at full frequency, inducing massive EMF and resulting in low impedance, drawing massive current from the mains.

T03_Motors.q: Why does the high starting current decay as the motor accelerates?
T03_Motors.a: As speed increases, slip decreases, reducing the rate of flux cutting and the induced rotor EMF
opts: As speed increases, slip decreases, reducing the rate of flux cutting and the induced rotor EMF
Because the stator winding heats up and increases resistance
Because the overload relay begins to actuate
T03_Motors.exp: As the rotor catches up to the RMF, relative speed (slip) drops, meaning Faraday induction weakens. Less EMF means less rotor current, reducing stator current demand.

T03_Motors.q: Which starting method provides the MAXIMUM starting torque?
T03_Motors.a: Direct-On-Line (DOL)
T03_Motors.exp: DOL applies full 100% supply voltage immediately. Since torque is proportional to the square of voltage (V²), full voltage gives maximum starting torque.

T03_Motors.q: What is the main disadvantage of DOL starting for large motors on ships?
T03_Motors.a: It causes a severe voltage dip on the ship's busbar, affecting other equipment
opts: It takes too long to start
It causes a severe voltage dip on the ship's busbar, affecting other equipment
It reduces the motor's running efficiency
T03_Motors.exp: Ship generator capacity is limited. A massive 6x current surge from a large pump starting DOL can pull down bus voltage, causing lights to dim and other contactors to drop out.

T03_Motors.q: By what factor does a Star-Delta starter reduce the starting current drawn from the line?
T03_Motors.a: 1/3 of the DOL line current
T03_Motors.exp: In star, phase voltage is reduced by 1/√3. Therefore, phase current is reduced by 1/√3. Line current equals phase current in star, making total line current 1/3 of the delta equivalent.

T03_Motors.q: How does a Star-Delta starter affect starting torque?
T03_Motors.a: Torque is reduced to 1/3 of the DOL starting torque
opts: Torque is reduced to 1/3 of the DOL starting torque
T03_Motors.exp: Motor torque is proportional to the square of the applied voltage (T ∝ V²). Since voltage in star is 1/√3, torque is (1/√3)² = 1/3.

T03_Motors.q: In a Star-Delta starter, how many terminals must the motor have in its terminal box?
T03_Motors.a: 6 terminals (both ends of all three phase windings must be accessible)
opts: 6 terminals (both ends of all three phase windings must be accessible)
T03_Motors.exp: The contactors in the starter panel must be able to reconfigure the windings from a Y (star) point to a delta loop, requiring access to U1-U2, V1-V2, and W1-W2.

T03_Motors.q: Which contactors are closed during the STAR phase of starting?
T03_Motors.a: Main contactor (KM) and Star contactor (KY)
T03_Motors.exp: KM connects the supply to U1/V1/W1. KY short-circuits U2/V2/W2 together to form the star point.

T03_Motors.q: What prevents the Star (KY) and Delta (KD) contactors from closing at the same time?
T03_Motors.a: Mechanical and electrical interlocks
T03_Motors.exp: If KY and KD close simultaneously, it creates a dead short circuit across the 3-phase supply. Interlocks make this physically and electrically impossible.

T03_Motors.q: What is the purpose of the 'Dead Time' (20-50ms) in a Star-Delta transition?
T03_Motors.a: To allow the motor's residual magnetic field to decay and prevent a massive out-of-phase transient current when Delta closes
opts: To let the motor cool down
To allow the motor's residual magnetic field to decay and prevent a massive out-of-phase transient current when Delta closes
To allow the timer relay to reset
To ensure the mechanical brake is released
T03_Motors.exp: When Star opens, the spinning rotor acts like a generator. If Delta closes instantly, the supply voltage and the motor's back-EMF may clash out of phase, causing a huge current spike.

T03_Motors.q: If a Star-Delta timer is set too short, what happens?
T03_Motors.a: The motor hasn't reached sufficient speed, causing a massive current surge when Delta closes
opts: The motor hasn't reached sufficient speed, causing a massive current surge when Delta closes
The star contactor burns out instantly
T03_Motors.exp: The purpose of Star is to accelerate the motor near full speed where slip is low. Transitioning too early defeats the purpose, acting like a delayed DOL start.

T03_Motors.q: If a Star-Delta timer is set too long, what happens?
T03_Motors.a: The motor stops accelerating at a lower speed (due to 1/3 torque) and just sits there drawing star current until transition
opts: The motor stops accelerating at a lower speed (due to 1/3 torque) and just sits there drawing star current until transition
The delta contactor will refuse to close
T03_Motors.exp: Because torque is only 1/3, the motor may hit an equilibrium with the load (e.g., a pump) before full speed. Delaying the transition further achieves nothing.

T03_Motors.q: Can a Star-Delta starter be used for a heavy loaded crane hoist?
T03_Motors.a: No, because starting torque is reduced to 1/3, it will fail to lift the load
opts: Yes, it is the standard for cranes
No, because starting torque is reduced to 1/3, it will fail to lift the load
Yes, but only if the timer is set very long
No, because cranes require DC power
T03_Motors.exp: Star-Delta is only suitable for motors starting unloaded or with light loads (fans, centrifugal pumps with discharge valve closed).

T03_Motors.q: How does an Auto-Transformer starter reduce starting voltage?
T03_Motors.a: By using a transformer with multiple tapping points (e.g., 65%, 80%) to step down the supply voltage
opts: By adding resistors in series with the stator
By using a transformer with multiple tapping points (e.g., 65%, 80%) to step down the supply voltage
By switching from star to delta
T03_Motors.exp: An autotransformer physically steps down the AC voltage applied to the motor during start, reducing current proportionally.

T03_Motors.q: What is the primary advantage of an Auto-Transformer starter over a Star-Delta starter?
T03_Motors.a: The starting voltage/torque can be adjusted (via taps) to suit the load, and transition is closed-circuit without current spikes
opts: The starting voltage/torque can be adjusted (via taps) to suit the load, and transition is closed-circuit without current spikes
T03_Motors.exp: Korndorfer transition keeps a portion of the autotransformer in circuit during the switch to full voltage, eliminating the 'dead time' current transient of Star-Delta.

T03_Motors.q: What internal electronic components are used in a Soft Starter to control voltage?
T03_Motors.a: Thyristors (SCRs) connected in anti-parallel pairs for each phase
opts: Thyristors (SCRs) connected in anti-parallel pairs for each phase
T03_Motors.exp: By delaying the firing angle of the thyristors (phase control), the soft starter chops the AC waveform, reducing the RMS voltage applied to the motor.

T03_Motors.q: Does a Soft Starter change the frequency of the supply?
T03_Motors.a: No, it only alters the RMS voltage
opts: Yes, it lowers frequency to start
No, it only alters the RMS voltage
Yes, it changes frequency and voltage together
Yes, it converts AC to pure DC
T03_Motors.exp: Soft starters only chop the 50Hz waveform to reduce voltage. The fundamental frequency remains 50Hz.

T03_Motors.q: What happens in a Soft Starter once the motor reaches full speed?
T03_Motors.a: A bypass contactor closes to route power around the thyristors
opts: The thyristors switch to frequency control mode
A bypass contactor closes to route power around the thyristors
The motor automatically switches to delta
T03_Motors.exp: Running continuous current through thyristors generates heat (losses). Once started, a mechanical bypass contactor closes to eliminate these losses.

T03_Motors.q: What is a 'Soft Stop' feature on a soft starter?
T03_Motors.a: It gradually ramps down the voltage to slowly decelerate the motor, preventing 'water hammer' in pump systems
opts: It applies a DC brake instantly
It gradually ramps down the voltage to slowly decelerate the motor, preventing 'water hammer' in pump systems
T03_Motors.exp: Instead of immediately cutting power (DOL stop) which causes check valves to slam shut, a soft stop slowly reduces pump pressure.

T03_Motors.q: In a Slip Ring (Wound Rotor) motor starter, where is the external resistance added?
T03_Motors.a: In the rotor circuit via the slip rings and brushes
opts: In the rotor circuit via the slip rings and brushes
T03_Motors.exp: The 3-phase rotor winding is brought out to slip rings. A contactor panel progressively shorts out external resistor banks as the motor accelerates.

T03_Motors.q: Why does adding rotor resistance in a slip-ring motor increase starting torque?
T03_Motors.a: It improves the rotor power factor at standstill, bringing rotor current more into phase with the magnetic flux
opts: It increases the total current drawn from the supply
It improves the rotor power factor at standstill, bringing rotor current more into phase with the magnetic flux
T03_Motors.exp: At standstill, rotor frequency is high (50Hz), making rotor reactance (X) much higher than resistance (R). Adding external R reduces the phase angle delay, maximizing torque.

T03_Motors.q: Can you use a slip-ring starter on a standard squirrel cage motor?
T03_Motors.a: No, because the squirrel cage rotor has no external electrical connections
opts: No, because the squirrel cage rotor has no external electrical connections
Yes, if it is a double cage motor
Yes, if used with a VFD
T03_Motors.exp: The squirrel cage is permanently short-circuited internally. You cannot add resistance to its circuit.

T03_Motors.q: What happens if one of the three fuses blows while a DOL motor is running?
T03_Motors.a: The motor continues to run on two phases (single phasing), drawing heavy current and overheating rapidly
opts: The motor continues to run on two phases (single phasing), drawing heavy current and overheating rapidly
T03_Motors.exp: This is single phasing. The motor acts as a phase converter, drawing excessive current to maintain load torque, leading to rapid burnout.

T03_Motors.q: What is the primary function of a 'current limiting' feature in a soft starter?
T03_Motors.a: It halts the voltage ramp-up if the starting current hits a preset limit (e.g., 350% FLC)
opts: It restricts the running current of the motor
It limits the maximum speed of the motor
It halts the voltage ramp-up if the starting current hits a preset limit (e.g., 350% FLC)
It acts as a short circuit fuse
T03_Motors.exp: If a heavy load causes starting current to spike, the soft starter pauses the voltage ramp until the motor accelerates and current drops naturally.

T03_Motors.q: Which starting method provides the highest starting torque per amp of starting current?
T03_Motors.a: VFD (Variable Frequency Drive)
T03_Motors.exp: By starting at a very low frequency (e.g., 2Hz), a VFD keeps the motor operating in the low-slip, high-torque region of its curve from zero RPM, drawing minimal current.

T03_Motors.q: Why are some large compressors started using an 'unloader valve'?
T03_Motors.a: To allow the motor to start against zero mechanical load, reducing starting duration and thermal stress
opts: To allow the motor to start against zero mechanical load, reducing starting duration and thermal stress
To prevent the star contactor from opening
T03_Motors.exp: Starting a compressor against a closed system pressure requires immense torque. The unloader vents the pressure to atmosphere until the motor is at full speed.

T03_Motors.q: In a DOL starter circuit, what is the purpose of the 'retaining' or 'hold-in' contact?
T03_Motors.a: It bypasses the start button, keeping the contactor coil energised after the button is released
opts: It connects the third phase to the motor
It trips the motor during overload
It bypasses the start button, keeping the contactor coil energised after the button is released
T03_Motors.exp: A Normally Open (NO) auxiliary contact on the main contactor is wired in parallel with the Start button. When KM closes, this contact closes, maintaining the control circuit.

T03_Motors.q: Why is 'under-voltage' protection inherent in a standard DOL contactor starter?
T03_Motors.a: If supply voltage drops too low, the contactor coil loses magnetic pull and drops out, disconnecting the motor
opts: Because it has a special UV relay
If supply voltage drops too low, the contactor coil loses magnetic pull and drops out, disconnecting the motor
Because the motor's back EMF shuts it off
Because the thermal overload strip cools down
T03_Motors.exp: A contactor coil requires a minimum voltage (usually ~80%) to hold the armature against the spring. In a blackout, it physically drops out.

T03_Motors.q: What must you do after a blackout to restart a pump on a standard DOL starter?
T03_Motors.a: You must physically press the start button again, as the retaining contact opened when power was lost
opts: You must physically press the start button again, as the retaining contact opened when power was lost
T03_Motors.exp: This is a crucial safety feature. It prevents massive simultaneous starting currents if power is restored, and protects personnel working on 'dead' machinery.

T03_Motors.q: What is 'Sequential Restart' after a blackout?
T03_Motors.a: A timer-based system that automatically restarts critical pumps in a staggered sequence to prevent generator overload
opts: A timer-based system that automatically restarts critical pumps in a staggered sequence to prevent generator overload
Starting the star contactor before delta
T03_Motors.exp: Essential services (LO pumps, SW pumps) have timers (e.g., 5s, 10s, 15s) in their control circuits so they don't all attempt DOL starts simultaneously when bus voltage is restored.

T03_Motors.q: What is the fundamental working principle of a Variable Frequency Drive (VFD)?
T03_Motors.a: It converts incoming AC to DC, then inverts it back to a synthetic AC waveform with variable voltage and frequency
opts: It uses transformers to step down voltage
It converts incoming AC to DC, then inverts it back to a synthetic AC waveform with variable voltage and frequency
It adds resistors to the stator winding
It mechanically changes the number of motor poles
T03_Motors.exp: The VFD consists of a Rectifier (AC to DC), a DC Link (filters the DC), and an Inverter (DC back to AC using PWM).

T03_Motors.q: Why must a VFD control both Voltage AND Frequency simultaneously (constant V/f ratio)?
T03_Motors.a: To maintain a constant magnetic flux in the air gap and prevent core saturation
opts: To increase the motor speed beyond sync speed
To maintain a constant magnetic flux in the air gap and prevent core saturation
To eliminate the need for a cooling fan
To convert the motor into a generator
T03_Motors.exp: Magnetic flux (Φ) is proportional to V/f. If you lower frequency to slow the motor but keep voltage high, flux becomes massive, saturating the iron core and burning out the stator.

T03_Motors.q: What technique does the VFD Inverter section use to recreate an AC waveform?
T03_Motors.a: Pulse Width Modulation (PWM) using IGBTs
T03_Motors.exp: Insulated Gate Bipolar Transistors (IGBTs) switch the DC voltage on and off thousands of times per second. Varying the pulse width creates an RMS current that looks like a sine wave to the motor.

T03_Motors.q: How does a VFD achieve full starting torque at near-zero RPM?
T03_Motors.a: By supplying a very low frequency (e.g. 1 Hz) and proportionally low voltage, operating the motor at optimal slip
opts: By supplying a very low frequency (e.g. 1 Hz) and proportionally low voltage, operating the motor at optimal slip
T03_Motors.exp: At 1Hz, the RMF spins very slowly. The rotor can easily slip slightly behind this slow RMF, producing massive torque without demanding high current.

T03_Motors.q: What is the primary drawback of using VFDs on ships?
T03_Motors.a: They generate high-frequency electrical harmonics that can distort the ship's power supply
opts: They can only run the motor at one speed
They generate high-frequency electrical harmonics that can distort the ship's power supply
T03_Motors.exp: The non-linear switching of the rectifier draws current in pulses, creating 5th, 7th, 11th, etc., harmonics. These must be mitigated using active or passive harmonic filters.

T03_Motors.q: What issue can VFDs cause to motor bearings?
T03_Motors.a: High-frequency PWM switching induces shaft voltages that can arc through the bearing grease, causing fluting
opts: They make the bearings run too cold
High-frequency PWM switching induces shaft voltages that can arc through the bearing grease, causing fluting
They melt the grease through radiation
T03_Motors.exp: Common-mode voltage from PWM induces a voltage on the rotor. If it exceeds the dielectric breakdown of the grease film, it arcs, leaving washboard-like pits (fluting) on the bearing races.

T03_Motors.q: How can you prevent bearing fluting caused by VFDs?
T03_Motors.a: Install a shaft grounding ring (e.g., AEGIS ring) to safely conduct shaft currents to earth
opts: Install a shaft grounding ring (e.g., AEGIS ring) to safely conduct shaft currents to earth
T03_Motors.exp: A shaft grounding ring uses carbon microfibers riding on the shaft to provide a low-impedance path to ground, bypassing the bearings entirely.

T03_Motors.q: Why do VFD-driven motors often require an external, independently powered cooling fan?
T03_Motors.a: Because running the motor at low speeds drastically reduces the cooling efficiency of the shaft-mounted fan
opts: Because VFDs generate heat in the surrounding air
Because running the motor at low speeds drastically reduces the cooling efficiency of the shaft-mounted fan
T03_Motors.exp: A motor running at 20% speed has 1/5th the cooling airflow. But if it's still producing high torque, it generates full heat. An independent fan ensures cooling regardless of motor speed.

T03_Motors.q: What is a 'Braking Chopper' and 'Braking Resistor' in a VFD system?
T03_Motors.a: Components used to dissipate regenerated energy as heat when decelerating a high-inertia load
opts: Components that physically brake the shaft
Components used to dissipate regenerated energy as heat when decelerating a high-inertia load
T03_Motors.exp: When a crane lowers a load, the motor acts as a generator. The VFD's DC link voltage spikes. The chopper switches this excess DC voltage to a large resistor bank to burn it off.

T03_Motors.q: What is the alternative to a Braking Resistor for handling regenerated energy in modern cranes?
T03_Motors.a: An Active Front End (AFE) VFD which feeds the regenerated power back into the ship's grid
opts: An Active Front End (AFE) VFD which feeds the regenerated power back into the ship's grid
T03_Motors.exp: AFE drives use IGBTs in the rectifier section instead of diodes, allowing bidirectional power flow, saving massive amounts of energy during cargo operations.

T03_Motors.q: Can a VFD drive a motor faster than its rated synchronous speed?
T03_Motors.a: Yes, by increasing the frequency above the baseline (e.g., to 60Hz or higher), operating in the field-weakening region
opts: Yes, by increasing the frequency above the baseline (e.g., to 60Hz or higher), operating in the field-weakening region
Yes, but only if voltage is increased to 1000V
T03_Motors.exp: Above 50Hz, the VFD cannot increase voltage further (limited to mains). Thus, V/f ratio drops (field weakening). Torque decreases, but power remains constant.

T03_Motors.q: Besides VFD, what is 'Pole Changing' (Dahlander) speed control?

T03_Motors.q: What is the Ward-Leonard system used for?

T03_Motors.q: What happens if the DC field excitation is lost in a DC motor while it is running?

To provide cooling to the armature

T03_Motors.exp: As the motor heats up, the inner ring on the hot shaft expands faster than the outer ring. A C3 clearance prevents the bearing from seizing due to thermal expansion.

T03_Motors.q: What is the primary function of a thermal overload relay (OLR) in a motor starter?
T03_Motors.a: To protect against sustained overcurrents (overheating) using a bimetallic strip
opts: To protect against sustained overcurrents (overheating) using a bimetallic strip
T03_Motors.exp: The OLR mimics the thermal characteristic of the motor. High current bends a bimetallic strip, eventually tripping the control circuit. It has an IDMT (Inverse Definite Minimum Time) characteristic.

T03_Motors.q: Why will a thermal overload relay NOT protect a motor against a short circuit?
T03_Motors.a: It responds too slowly (thermal time delay); short circuits require instantaneous clearing
opts: It is not connected to the main power lines
It responds too slowly (thermal time delay); short circuits require instantaneous clearing
T03_Motors.exp: An OLR takes seconds or minutes to trip. A short circuit (thousands of amps) will melt the wires before the bimetallic strip bends. Short circuits are cleared by Fuses or Magnetic MCBs.

T03_Motors.q: What type of fuse is mandatory for 440V motor feeders on the Main Switchboard?
T03_Motors.a: HRC (High Rupturing Capacity) Fuses
T03_Motors.exp: HRC fuses can safely interrupt massive fault currents (e.g., 80kA) without exploding, thanks to the arc-quenching silica sand inside.

T03_Motors.q: At what rating are motor HRC fuses typically selected compared to the Full Load Current (FLC)?
T03_Motors.a: 1.5 to 2.5 times the motor FLC
T03_Motors.exp: The fuse must NOT blow during the massive 6x DOL starting current surge. Therefore, they are rated higher than FLC. The OLR handles the slight overloads.

T03_Motors.q: How does a 3-element overload relay provide 'Single Phasing' protection?
T03_Motors.a: It uses a differential mechanism that trips much faster if one bimetallic strip cools down while the others heat up
opts: It measures the phase voltage directly
It uses a differential mechanism that trips much faster if one bimetallic strip cools down while the others heat up
It has a built in fuse for each phase
T03_Motors.exp: If one phase is lost, its strip cools and straightens. The other two carry 2x current and bend aggressively. A mechanical slide bar detects this differential and trips rapidly.

T03_Motors.q: What is the consequence of single-phasing a motor that is currently STOPPED?
T03_Motors.a: The motor will hum loudly but will not rotate, and will quickly burn out if not tripped
opts: It will start normally but run slowly
The motor will hum loudly but will not rotate, and will quickly burn out if not tripped
T03_Motors.exp: Two phases cannot create a Rotating Magnetic Field, only a pulsating field. Starting torque is strictly zero.

T03_Motors.q: What causes the 'Negative Sequence Currents' during single-phasing?
T03_Motors.a: The unbalanced voltage creates a counter-rotating magnetic field that induces high frequency currents in the rotor
opts: The unbalanced voltage creates a counter-rotating magnetic field that induces high frequency currents in the rotor
T03_Motors.exp: The pulsating field can be mathematically split into a forward RMF and a backward RMF. The backward RMF spins at 2x slip frequency relative to the rotor, causing immense localized heating.

T03_Motors.q: Besides the OLR, what electronic relay offers superior protection against single-phasing and phase reversal?
T03_Motors.a: Phase Failure / Phase Sequence Relay
T03_Motors.exp: This relay directly monitors the 3-phase voltage waveform. If a phase drops, or if the sequence is reversed (which would run the pump backwards), it instantly opens the control circuit.

T03_Motors.q: Why do large ER motors have PTC thermistors embedded in the stator windings?
T03_Motors.a: To provide direct thermal protection by measuring actual winding temperature, regardless of current draw
opts: To provide direct thermal protection by measuring actual winding temperature, regardless of current draw
To control the speed of the VFD
T03_Motors.exp: If the motor cooling fan fails, or filter is blocked, the motor will overheat even if drawing normal current. The OLR won't see this, but the thermistors will spike in resistance and trip the motor.

T03_Motors.q: What is the function of the Anti-Condensation Heater (Space Heater) in a motor?
T03_Motors.a: It turns on automatically when the motor STOPS, keeping windings warm to prevent moisture condensation
opts: It pre-heats the bearings before starting
It turns on automatically when the motor STOPS, keeping windings warm to prevent moisture condensation
It warms the fuel oil for the pump
T03_Motors.exp: When a hot motor stops, cooling draws in humid ER air. If it cools below the dew point, water condenses on the windings, ruining insulation. The heater prevents this.

T03_Motors.q: Where does the Anti-Condensation Heater get its power?
T03_Motors.a: Usually from an independent 220V supply, interlocked via a normally-closed (NC) contact of the main contactor
opts: Usually from an independent 220V supply, interlocked via a normally-closed (NC) contact of the main contactor
T03_Motors.exp: When KM is open (motor off), the NC auxiliary contact is closed, feeding 220V to the heater. 🔴 DANGER: This means 220V is LIVE inside the terminal box even when the 440V breaker is off!

T03_Motors.q: How does a Core Balance Current Transformer (CBCT) detect an earth fault in a motor?
T03_Motors.a: It wraps around all 3 phase cables; if no leakage exists, the vector sum of currents is zero
opts: It measures voltage to the hull
It wraps around all 3 phase cables; if no leakage exists, the vector sum of currents is zero
It measures the resistance of the earth cable
It detects smoke in the terminal box
T03_Motors.exp: Normally, whatever current goes down R and Y returns via B. The net magnetic field is zero. If current leaks to the hull (earth), the sum is no longer zero, inducing a signal in the CBCT.

T03_Motors.q: What is a 'Double Cage' (Double Squirrel Cage) Induction Motor?
T03_Motors.a: A motor with two sets of rotor bars: an outer high-resistance cage and an inner low-resistance cage
opts: A motor with two sets of rotor bars: an outer high-resistance cage and an inner low-resistance cage
A motor with physical safety guards
A slip ring motor without brushes
T03_Motors.exp: This clever design uses the 'skin effect' to automatically provide high torque during starting (outer cage) and high efficiency during running (inner cage) without external starters.

T03_Motors.q: Why does the rotor current flow primarily in the OUTER cage of a double cage motor during starting?
T03_Motors.a: At start, rotor frequency is 50Hz. High frequency pushes current to the surface (skin effect) into the high-resistance outer bars
opts: Because the inner cage is disconnected by a switch
At start, rotor frequency is 50Hz. High frequency pushes current to the surface (skin effect) into the high-resistance outer bars
Because the outer cage has less resistance
T03_Motors.exp: The inner cage is deeply buried, giving it massive inductive reactance (XL = 2πfL) at 50Hz. Current takes the path of least impedance: the outer cage.

T03_Motors.q: Where are Double Cage motors typically used on ships?
T03_Motors.a: For machinery requiring High Starting Torque without complex starters: Windlass, Mooring Winches, Bow Thrusters
opts: For machinery requiring High Starting Torque without complex starters: Windlass, Mooring Winches, Bow Thrusters
T03_Motors.exp: A windlass must start against massive chain tension. A double cage gives excellent DOL starting torque without the need for delicate slip rings.

T03_Motors.q: What phenomenon causes 'Motor Crawling'?
T03_Motors.a: The 7th harmonic in the air-gap flux creates a forward-rotating field at 1/7th synchronous speed, forming a reluctance torque dip
opts: The 7th harmonic in the air-gap flux creates a forward-rotating field at 1/7th synchronous speed, forming a reluctance torque dip
T03_Motors.exp: If the mechanical load torque is higher than this 'dip' in the motor's torque curve, the motor gets stuck at 1/7th speed (e.g., 200 RPM instead of 1450 RPM).

T03_Motors.q: How is Motor Crawling prevented during motor manufacture?
T03_Motors.a: By skewing the rotor slots and properly chording the stator windings to eliminate the 7th harmonic
opts: By making the air gap larger
By skewing the rotor slots and properly chording the stator windings to eliminate the 7th harmonic
T03_Motors.exp: Skewing breaks up the harmonic alignment. Chording (short-pitching) the stator coils cancels out specific spatial harmonics in the flux.

T03_Motors.q: If a Surveyor asks: 'What specs do you provide when ordering a new motor?', which of these is the most complete answer?

opts: kW, Voltage, Hz, Poles/RPM, Frame Size, IP Rating, Insulation Class, Mounting type (B3/B5)
T03_Motors.exp: A motor cannot be replaced unless the physical dimensions (Frame, Mounting) and environmental limits (IP, Class) match, alongside the electrical specs.

T03_Motors.q: What is the difference between a B3 and B5 motor mounting?
T03_Motors.a: B3 is Foot-mounted; B5 is Flange-mounted

B3 is Foot-mounted; B5 is Flange-mounted
B3 is waterproof; B5 is not
B3 requires a VFD; B5 is DOL

T03_Motors.q: When a motor returns from shore after rewinding, what is the first electrical check the ETO must perform?

Insulation Resistance test (Megger) between all phases and earth

T03_Motors.q: After rewinding, why must you measure the DC resistance of all three phases with a low-resistance bridge?

To ensure Resistance Balance; all phases must be equal within 2% to prevent unbalanced magnetic pull and heating
T03_Motors.exp: If the winder used the wrong wire gauge or fewer turns on one phase, the resistance will differ, causing severe issues under load.

T03_Motors.q: What tool is used to confirm the correct U-V-W connection sequence before coupling a newly installed motor?
T03_Motors.a: A Phase Rotation Meter
T03_Motors.exp: Running a pump backwards can unscrew the impeller or destroy the mechanical seal instantly. You must verify the supply phase sequence matches the motor's intended rotation.

opts: Dust tight (6) and suitable for continuous submersion in water (8)
T03_Motors.exp: A standard engine room motor is IP44. An exposed deck motor is IP55/56. Only IP68 guarantees survival if fully submerged in the bilges.

T03_Motors.q: If a Main Cooling Sea Water (MCSW) pump motor is built with Class F insulation (155°C max), at what temperature is it typically designed to operate?

opts: Class B temperature limits (130°C) to provide a 25°C safety margin for reliability
T03_Motors.exp: Marine classification societies prefer 'Class F insulated, Class B rise'. This thermal buffer ensures long life in harsh, high-ambient engine rooms.

T03_Motors.q: What does 'Ex d' indicate on a hazardous area motor's nameplate?

T03_Motors.q: A surveyor asks: 'A 440V motor is repeatedly tripping on its thermal overload relay. The load is normal. What is the most likely electrical cause?'
T03_Motors.a: A high resistance contact in one of the starter contactors, causing an unbalanced phase voltage
opts: The motor's cooling fan is blocked
A high resistance contact in one of the starter contactors, causing an unbalanced phase voltage
The motor's insulation resistance is 2 Megohms
The supply frequency has dropped to 49Hz
T03_Motors.exp: A pitted or burned contact in the main contactor (KM) creates a voltage drop on one phase. This phase imbalance causes severe negative sequence currents, massively increasing rotor heating and causing the OLR to trip even if the mechanical load is normal.

T03_Motors.q: How can you differentiate between a thermal overload trip and a magnetic short-circuit trip when a motor stops unexpectedly?
T03_Motors.a: An OLR trip can be reset after a few minutes of cooling; a short-circuit trip usually throws an MCB or blows an HRC fuse
opts: An OLR trip can be reset after a few minutes of cooling; a short-circuit trip usually throws an MCB or blows an HRC fuse
A short circuit trip will reset automatically
An OLR trip destroys the motor
T03_Motors.exp: The bimetallic strip in an OLR requires time to cool before the reset mechanism engages. An MCB or fuse trips instantly and requires physical replacement or manual lever reset.

T03_Motors.q: You start a massive engine room ventilation fan via a Star-Delta starter. It accelerates in Star, but the moment it switches to Delta, the main breaker trips. Why?
T03_Motors.a: The transition timer was set too short, so the motor had not reached sufficient speed, causing a massive DOL-like current surge in Delta
opts: The transition timer was set too short, so the motor had not reached sufficient speed, causing a massive DOL-like current surge in Delta
The delta contactor is wired in reverse
The star contactor failed to open
T03_Motors.exp: If the timer is too short, the slip is still very high when Delta closes. Applying full 440V at high slip results in a massive current surge that trips the magnetic short-circuit protection.

T03_Motors.q: What happens if the 'Dead Time' in a Star-Delta transition is completely eliminated (i.e., Star opens and Delta closes instantly)?
T03_Motors.a: The residual back-EMF of the motor may clash out-of-phase with the supply voltage, creating a devastating transient current
opts: The motor runs smoothly without interruption
The residual back-EMF of the motor may clash out-of-phase with the supply voltage, creating a devastating transient current
T03_Motors.exp: The spinning motor temporarily acts as a generator. If Delta closes while this back-EMF is out of phase with the grid, the resulting transient current can exceed 15x full load current, ripping windings apart.

T03_Motors.q: A surveyor asks: 'How do you check if a 3-phase induction motor has a burnt-out (open circuit) stator winding using a multimeter?'
T03_Motors.a: Measure the resistance across U1-U2, V1-V2, and W1-W2; one phase will show infinite resistance
opts: Measure the resistance between U1 and earth
Measure the resistance across U1-U2, V1-V2, and W1-W2; one phase will show infinite resistance
Check the voltage at the terminal box
T03_Motors.exp: An open circuit means the copper wire has broken (burnt through). A standard multimeter will show infinite resistance (OL) across the ends of the broken phase winding.

T03_Motors.q: What is the critical danger of attempting to restart a large motor immediately after it has tripped on thermal overload?
T03_Motors.a: The copper windings are already extremely hot; a starting current surge of 6x FLC will likely melt the insulation and destroy the motor
opts: The copper windings are already extremely hot; a starting current surge of 6x FLC will likely melt the insulation and destroy the motor
The power factor will drop to zero
T03_Motors.exp: Heat is cumulative. If it just tripped on overload, the internal hotspot temperature is near the limit (e.g., 155°C). Hitting it with a 50A starting surge adds massive I²R heat, pushing it past the breakdown point.

T03_Motors.q: Why is it absolutely forbidden to use a standard Megger (Insulation Resistance Tester) on a motor connected to a Variable Frequency Drive (VFD)?
T03_Motors.a: The 500V DC injected by the Megger will destroy the sensitive IGBTs and diodes in the VFD's inverter and rectifier sections
opts: The Megger will not read accurately
The 500V DC injected by the Megger will destroy the sensitive IGBTs and diodes in the VFD's inverter and rectifier sections
The VFD will absorb the DC and charge its capacitors
T03_Motors.exp: Solid-state electronics cannot withstand high DC test voltages. You must physically disconnect the motor cables from the VFD terminals before meggering the motor.

T03_Motors.q: A 3-phase motor is heavily vibrating and emitting a loud, pulsing 100Hz hum. The mechanical coupling is perfectly aligned. What is the electrical fault?
T03_Motors.a: Single phasing or severe voltage imbalance causing a negative sequence counter-rotating magnetic field
opts: Single phasing or severe voltage imbalance causing a negative sequence counter-rotating magnetic field
T03_Motors.exp: When a phase is lost, the pulsating magnetic field creates a severe 'unbalanced magnetic pull' (UMP) that tugs the rotor violently at twice the supply frequency, causing intense vibration.

T03_Motors.q: You are meggering a newly arrived motor from the shore workshop. The IR reading is 0.2 MΩ. What must you do?
T03_Motors.a: Do not energize it; place it in a dry, warm place or apply low DC voltage to bake out the absorbed moisture until IR exceeds 1 MΩ
opts: Energize it immediately to heat it up
Do not energize it; place it in a dry, warm place or apply low DC voltage to bake out the absorbed moisture until IR exceeds 1 MΩ
T03_Motors.exp: 0.2 MΩ indicates severe moisture absorption during transit. Applying 440V will cause an instant flashover to earth. It must be dried (varnish baked) first.

T03_Motors.q: A motor is running perfectly, but the external casing feels excessively hot to the touch. Current draw is normal. What should you check first?
T03_Motors.a: Check if the cooling fan cowl is blocked by dirt, or if the external cooling fins are caked in grease/paint
opts: Check if the cooling fan cowl is blocked by dirt, or if the external cooling fins are caked in grease/paint
T03_Motors.exp: TEFC (Totally Enclosed Fan Cooled) motors rely entirely on the external fan blowing air over the ribbed fins. If the fins are choked with dust/oil, the heat cannot escape.

T03_Motors.q: What happens to a squirrel cage induction motor if two phases of the supply are swapped while it is running at full speed?
T03_Motors.a: It undergoes 'Plugging' — brutal deceleration as it tries to reverse instantly, drawing massive current and potentially shearing the shaft
opts: It undergoes 'Plugging' — brutal deceleration as it tries to reverse instantly, drawing massive current and potentially shearing the shaft
It trips the earth fault relay
T03_Motors.exp: Swapping phases reverses the RMF direction. The rotor (spinning at +1450 RPM) is suddenly facing an RMF at -1500 RPM. Slip becomes ~200%. The mechanical and electrical shock is catastrophic.

T03_Motors.q: Why do surveyors emphasize checking the 'Air Gap' using a long feeler gauge during a major motor overhaul?
T03_Motors.a: To ensure the rotor is perfectly centralized within the stator; an uneven gap causes Unbalanced Magnetic Pull (UMP) and destroys bearings
opts: To ensure the rotor is perfectly centralized within the stator; an uneven gap causes Unbalanced Magnetic Pull (UMP) and destroys bearings
To measure the thickness of the insulation
To ensure the cooling air can flow freely
T03_Motors.exp: As the rotor spins, if it is closer to the stator at the 6 o'clock position (due to bearing wear or poor end-shield alignment), the magnetic pull there is vastly stronger, bending the shaft.

T03_Motors.q: What is the function of the 'Centrifugal Switch' in a single-phase induction motor?
T03_Motors.a: It disconnects the high-resistance starting winding once the motor reaches about 75% of synchronous speed
opts: It shuts off the motor if it spins too fast
It disconnects the high-resistance starting winding once the motor reaches about 75% of synchronous speed
It switches the motor to delta connection
T03_Motors.exp: Single-phase motors have no natural rotating field. A starting winding (with a capacitor) creates an artificial phase shift to start. Once spinning, the main winding sustains rotation, and the starting winding is removed to prevent burnout.

T03_Motors.q: You find a motor's bearing housing extremely hot and 'weeping' oil, but the motor casing itself is cool. What is the diagnosis?
T03_Motors.a: Over-greasing. The bearing cavity is fully packed, causing extreme fluid friction (churning) which overheats and separates the grease
opts: Over-greasing. The bearing cavity is fully packed, causing extreme fluid friction (churning) which overheats and separates the grease
T03_Motors.exp: Grease consists of oil suspended in a soap matrix. Massive churning heat from over-greasing breaks down the matrix, bleeding the oil out and leaving behind a hard crust that ruins the bearing.

T03_Motors.q: If a ship is supplied with 60Hz power, but you install a motor designed strictly for 50Hz, what will happen?
T03_Motors.a: The motor will run 20% faster, potentially overloading the driven pump/fan due to the cube law of power
opts: The motor will run 20% faster, potentially overloading the driven pump/fan due to the cube law of power
T03_Motors.exp: Ns = 120f/P. Increasing frequency to 60Hz increases speed by 60/50 (1.2x). For a centrifugal pump, power required is proportional to speed cubed (1.2³ = 1.72). The motor will draw 72% more power and trip.

T03_Motors.q: How does an 'Active Front End' (AFE) VFD differ from a standard VFD when dealing with a descending crane load?
T03_Motors.a: It uses IGBTs in the rectifier to push regenerated AC power back into the ship's grid, instead of burning it in a resistor
opts: It uses IGBTs in the rectifier to push regenerated AC power back into the ship's grid, instead of burning it in a resistor
It applies a DC injection to stop the motor
It increases the frequency to brake
T03_Motors.exp: Standard rectifiers use diodes (one-way flow). AFE rectifiers use synchronized IGBTs, allowing bi-directional power flow, making them highly energy-efficient for heavy lifting applications.

T03_Motors.q: What is the purpose of 'Chording' (Short-pitching) the stator windings in an AC motor?
T03_Motors.a: To eliminate specific spatial harmonics (like the 5th and 7th) from the magnetic flux, preventing crawling and reducing losses
opts: To eliminate specific spatial harmonics (like the 5th and 7th) from the magnetic flux, preventing crawling and reducing losses
To allow the motor to run on DC power
T03_Motors.exp: By making the span of a coil slightly less than a full pole pitch, the fundamental voltages add up efficiently, but the higher-order harmonic voltages cancel each other out.

T03_Motors.q: Why is 'Skewing' the rotor bars a standard practice in squirrel cage motors?
T03_Motors.a: It reduces magnetic humming (noise) and eliminates 'cogging' (magnetic locking of stator and rotor teeth)
opts: It reduces magnetic humming (noise) and eliminates 'cogging' (magnetic locking of stator and rotor teeth)
T03_Motors.exp: If the bars were perfectly straight, they would align exactly with the stator slots, causing strong magnetic attraction (cogging) at standstill. Skewing breaks this alignment, ensuring smooth starting torque.

T03_Motors.q: A surveyor asks: 'A pump motor is drawing normal current but the flow rate is very low. The motor was recently replaced. What is the cause?'
T03_Motors.a: The phase sequence is reversed, causing the motor and impeller to run backwards
opts: The phase sequence is reversed, causing the motor and impeller to run backwards
T03_Motors.exp: A centrifugal pump running backwards will still move water, but at a vastly reduced flow and pressure, while drawing seemingly normal current. Swap any two phases to fix.

T03_Motors.q: What is the correct procedure if a motor falls into the sea and is retrieved hours later?
T03_Motors.a: Wash thoroughly with fresh water to remove salt, bake in an oven at 80-100°C for hours/days until IR >1MΩ, then re-varnish
opts: Dry it with compressed air and start it immediately
Wash thoroughly with fresh water to remove salt, bake in an oven at 80-100°C for hours/days until IR >1MΩ, then re-varnish
Wash with diesel and megger it
Throw it away, it is unrecoverable
T03_Motors.exp: Salt is highly conductive and hygroscopic. It MUST be washed out with fresh water immediately. Only a slow, deep bake will drive out the moisture from the inner windings.

T03_Motors.q: What happens if a synchronous motor is 'under-excited' (DC field is too weak)?
T03_Motors.a: It will draw a lagging reactive current from the AC supply, acting like an inductor
opts: It will run faster than synchronous speed
It will draw a lagging reactive current from the AC supply, acting like an inductor
It will draw a leading current
It will switch to generating mode
T03_Motors.exp: An under-excited synchronous motor relies on the AC stator supply to make up the missing magnetic flux, drawing lagging VARs. If over-excited, it supplies leading VARs.

T03_Motors.q: In a slip-ring induction motor, what happens if the external rotor resistance is left IN the circuit during normal running?
T03_Motors.a: The motor will run at high slip (lower speed), and massive I²R heat will be generated in the resistors, wasting energy
opts: The motor will run at synchronous speed
The motor will run at high slip (lower speed), and massive I²R heat will be generated in the resistors, wasting energy
The starting torque will drop to zero
The power factor will improve to unity
T03_Motors.exp: External resistance is only for starting (to increase torque and lower current). Once running, it must be shorted out, otherwise it acts as a very inefficient speed controller, burning power as heat.

T03_Motors.q: What is the function of an 'Anti-Vibration Mount' or flexible rubber coupling between a motor and a pump?
T03_Motors.a: To absorb slight misalignments and prevent transmission of torsional shocks and vibrations between the shafts
opts: To absorb slight misalignments and prevent transmission of torsional shocks and vibrations between the shafts
To act as a heat sink
T03_Motors.exp: Even with precision laser alignment, thermal expansion causes shafts to shift during operation. A flexible coupling (e.g., spider insert) accommodates this microscopic movement without destroying the bearings.

T03_Motors.q: What is a 'Polarization Index' (PI) test for a high voltage motor?
T03_Motors.a: The ratio of the Megger reading at 10 minutes to the reading at 1 minute; it indicates the dryness and cleanliness of the insulation
opts: The ratio of the Megger reading at 10 minutes to the reading at 1 minute; it indicates the dryness and cleanliness of the insulation
The phase angle between voltage and current
The ratio of starting current to running current
T03_Motors.exp: A PI > 2.0 is generally acceptable. If insulation is dirty/wet, the leakage current remains high, and the ratio will be close to 1.0 (fail).

T03_Motors.q: Why should you never open the secondary circuit of a Current Transformer (CT) while the motor is running?
T03_Motors.a: It will induce a lethally high voltage across the open secondary terminals and destroy the CT insulation
opts: It will induce a lethally high voltage across the open secondary terminals and destroy the CT insulation
It will cause the motor to overspeed
It will blow the main fuses
T03_Motors.exp: A CT acts as a step-up transformer for voltage. If the secondary is open (infinite resistance), the secondary voltage spikes to thousands of volts attempting to push the proportional current.

T03_Motors.q: How does a 'Phase-Angle Control' thyristor soft starter limit current?
T03_Motors.a: It delays the firing pulse to the thyristor gate, only allowing a small portion of each AC half-wave to pass to the motor
opts: It delays the firing pulse to the thyristor gate, only allowing a small portion of each AC half-wave to pass to the motor
T03_Motors.exp: By chopping the waveform, the RMS (average) voltage is reduced. As the motor accelerates, the firing angle is advanced until full sine waves are passed.

T03_Motors.q: A motor nameplate lists a Service Factor (SF) of 1.15. What does this mean?
T03_Motors.a: The motor can operate continuously at 15% over its rated horsepower without catastrophic failure
opts: The motor can operate continuously at 15% over its rated horsepower without catastrophic failure
It will run 15% faster than nominal speed
T03_Motors.exp: An SF > 1.0 provides a buffer for short-term overloads or voltage fluctuations. However, running continuously in the service factor zone reduces the motor's lifespan due to higher heat.

T03_Motors.q: What is the danger of using a standard non-inverter duty motor with a VFD over a long cable run?
T03_Motors.a: Reflected waves (voltage spikes) can exceed the motor's insulation rating, causing the winding insulation to break down and short
opts: The cable will act as an antenna and transmit radio signals
Reflected waves (voltage spikes) can exceed the motor's insulation rating, causing the winding insulation to break down and short
The VFD will lose its programming
T03_Motors.exp: The sharp voltage pulses (dv/dt) from the VFD reflect back from the motor terminals, doubling the voltage peak (e.g., 1000V+ on a 440V line). 'Inverter Duty' motors have reinforced insulation.
